messages:
Morgan: FYI - ACME reported a sharp p99 jump starting ~03:15 UTC after a deploy. They see a lot of 401s from our auth gateway and p99 for text-gen endpoints jumped from ~220ms to ~2.8s. Can eng-sre triage?
Alex: Investigating logs now. Do we have tenant id / example request ids?
Morgan: Tenant acme-inc, recent request ids: rq_ee38a, rq_ee39b. Customer says spike correlates with a new SSO rollout on their side.
Jamie: I pulled traces for rq_ee38a - interesting: auth authn call to our token-introspect took ~800ms and then continuous-batcher held tiny requests for up to 1.6s before dispatch. Looks like auth delays + coalescing hold window = head-of-line tail.
Sam: That sounds like the continuous-batcher is using default hold_ms=1500 + max_batch_delay interactions. When upstream auth stalls, small payloads pile up behind a large hold period.
Lucy: Can we confirm API errors are returning 401 vs 5xx? Morgan said a few 5xx too.
Morgan: Mixed. Mostly 401 then some 502 from auth-proxy. Billing notice: customer on metered plan, high traffic.
Alex: Repro steps I used: curl to text-gen with invalid token repeatedly -> our auth-proxy does backoff and some requests queue. I can reproduce a p99 spike locally by forcing auth-introspect latency.
Jamie: Key observation: continuous-batcher tries to fill batch, but for tiny requests that means waiting hold window until either batch hits size or timeout. If auth introduces variable latency, hold window becomes the dominant contributor to p99.
Sam: Immediate mitigations we can try: 1) reduce continuous-batcher hold_ms for route acme-inc to 200ms 2) enable fast-path for small payloads (bypass coalesce when auth status unknown) 3) route requests with auth failure faster to fail-fast path so they don't block healthy requests.
Lucy: Which mitigation is lowest-risk to push quickly?
Alex: Reducing hold_ms for tenant-specific route is low risk. Patch config and can rollback in 2 mins.
Jamie: I have a canary config bundle:
```
route: /v1/generate
tenant: acme-inc
batching:
  mode: continuous
  hold_ms: 200
  max_batch_size: 8
```
Apply to 10% of their traffic first.
Sam: Also suggest temporary rule: if upstream auth takes >300ms, mark request as auth-slow and treat as fail-fast for coalescing (so it doesn't block). That's a small change in runtime but higher risk.
Morgan: Customer asked for timeline. If we can roll hold_ms change now that's best. They can also pause their SSO rollout.
Alex: I'll open a quick config change PR and request emergency rollout.
DeployBot: deploy request accepted: config-change/4790012345 -> canary 10% on route /v1/generate for tenant acme-inc.
Alex: Rolling now:
```
curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/v1/configs/apply \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer ${REDACTED}" \
 -d '{"target":"route:/v1/generate","tenant":"acme-inc","batching": {"hold_ms":200,"max_batch_size":8},"canary_pct":10}'
```
DeployBot: rollout started -> canary 10% (cfg id cfg_4790012345_canary).
Jamie: I'm watching p95/p99 on their route metrics.
Lucy: Also enable a quick metric alert for auth_error_rate > 1% so we can correlate.
BillingBot: Note: customer exceeded free tier credits; will surface billing notification but not relevant to latency fix.
Jamie: Canary results after 8m: p99 for canary down from ~2.8s to ~420ms. Non-canary remains elevated.
Alex: Good sign. Proceed to increase canary to 50%?
Sam: Yes, go to 50% but hold full rollout until auth errors subside. Also add a temporary rule to bypass coalesce for requests with status=auth_unknown.
DeployBot: updated rollout -> canary 50% (cfg id cfg_4790012345_canary).
Jamie: After 20m at 50% p99 down tenant-wide to ~360ms, overall customer SLA back to acceptable levels. Auth error rate still elevated but not blocking normal traffic now.
Morgan: Customer confirmed improved latency and is pausing SSO rollback. They want a postmortem and permanent config changes.
Lucy: Action items: 1) eng-runtime to add per-tenant hold_ms defaults and quick toggle (Sam, Jamie) 2) runtime change to mark auth-slow as non-coalescing (Jamie) 3) docs/update playbook for auth-induced batching tail (Alex) 4) follow up with customer success on communication (Morgan).
Sam: I'll open tickets: RUNTIME-892 (per-tenant batching defaults), RUNTIME-893 (auth-slow fast-path). Jamie will own 893.
Alex: I'll write short rollback + runbook and attach traces.
Morgan: Thanks. Closing this thread for now — will reopen if canary regresses. :thumbsup:
Lucy: One more note - consider adding a synthetic test that simulates auth latency to catch this during staging.
Jamie: Agreed, adding to test matrix.
Morgan: Thread closed.
